race.name: Chasing Cancellara Granfondo Vaduz
race.tagline: Five timed climbs inside a neutralized group ride linking Liechtenstein and eastern Switzerland.

vitals.course_status_reason: The organizer publishes complete results, roadbook, and route facts for April 25, 2026 but no 2027 date, registration cycle, rules, or course.
vitals.field_size: Not published for the next edition
vitals.prize_purse: Rankings are based on five timed climbs; no cash purse published
vitals.feed_zones: One on-course feed zone in the completed 2026 edition

climate.description: Late April in the Rhine valley can be mild, but rain and cool air remain realistic on the exposed climbs.

terrain.primary: Rolling paved loops with five timed climbs
terrain.surface: Paved public roads under neutralized group rules between timed climbing sectors.

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Grade uses the organizer's completed 2026 98 km / 1,290 m long loop, five timed climbs, neutralized transfers, roadbook, results, moto escort, medical support, neutral service, and feed-zone package. Formula: 37/70 = 53. Re-grade when the next edition is announced. Sources: https://www.chasingcancellara.com/granfondo-vaduz and its official 2026 roadbook.

distance.explanation: The 2026 long loop was 98 km, squarely inside the 80-120 km band.[2][3]

climbing.explanation: The organizer published 1,290 m for the long loop, inside the 500-1,500 m band.[2][3]

descent_technicality.explanation: Short, steep sectors require control but the event is not built around major alpine descents.[3]

road_surface.explanation: The roadbook describes public paved roads without cobbled or deteriorated showcase sectors.[3]

climate_risk.explanation: Late-April Alpine-foothill weather can bring cold rain and wind; this is a conservative editorial grade.[2]

altitude.explanation: The roadbook profile rises from Vaduz at 460 m to Pfäfers at roughly 820 m.[3]

logistics.explanation: Vaduz is orderly and compact but requires regional rail or road transfer from a major airport.[2]

prestige.explanation: Fabian Cancellara's brand gives the event recognition, but it remains a regional format.[1][2]

organization.explanation: Timing, moto escort, first aid, neutral service, guides, roadbook, and feed support meet the very-good band.[2][3]

scenic_experience.explanation: The Liechtenstein and eastern-Swiss loops are distinctive without a high-Alpine pass.[3]

community_culture.explanation: Group riding, a finisher meal, rankings, and series identity support a solid event community.[1][2]

field_depth.explanation: Five timed climbs and published rankings create structured competition.[2][3]

value.explanation: The package is substantial, but no next-edition fee exists for a stronger claim.[2]

expenses.explanation: Liechtenstein travel and lodging are not budget racing, though the loop format avoids point-to-point transfers.[2]

course_description.character: Riders travel together between five timed climbing sectors, with rankings decided by accumulated climb times. The completed 2026 long loop crossed Liechtenstein and eastern Switzerland before returning to Vaduz.
course_description.signature_challenge: Repeatedly switching from controlled group riding into five short, steep, fully timed climbing efforts.

logistics.airport: Zurich Airport (ZRH), followed by regional rail or road transfer to Vaduz
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Vaduz, Schaan, or nearby Buchs and keep race morning local.
logistics.transport: The loop starts and finishes in Vaduz; no finish-city transfer is required.
logistics.food: Organizer feed support and a finisher meal were included in 2026.

history.origin_story: Granfondo Vaduz is the short-format climbing race in Fabian Cancellara's three-event Swiss series.
notable_moments: 2026: 98 km long loop with five timed climbs and neutralized transfers
history.reputation: A compact, tactical alternative to the series' two ultra-distance point-to-point races.

biased_opinion.verdict: The Smart One in the Series
biased_opinion.summary: Vaduz keeps the competitive part honest—five timed climbs—but removes the 2:00 AM ultra-distance ordeal. It is the best Chasing Cancellara entry point for riders who want real rankings without spending all day crossing Switzerland.
weaknesses: Transfers are neutralized rather than raced
Less spectacular than the high-Alpine routes
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A well-produced climbing contest with manageable distance, but not ready for a dated training-plan product until the organizer announces the next edition.

final_verdict.one_liner: Five timed climbs, neutralized transfers, and a compact Vaduz loop.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a competitive climbing format without an ultra-distance day. Wait for the next edition before committing a training calendar.
final_verdict.alternatives: Chasing Cancellara Zürich-Andermatt and Bern-Zermatt trade compact logistics for true Alpine ultra distance.
